title: Trip Album Completion Lag
dataSources: Photos (`photo:capture`), places visited (`location:visit`), voice memos (`voicememo:note`), logged moments (`lifelog:moment`), timeline events (`timeline:event`).
app: Life-logging and memory telemetry — photo libraries (Google Photos, Immich), location history, voice memos, and daily-moment journals — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=photo:capture trip_name=* album_published_epoch=*
| stats max(_time) as last_photo, max(album_published_epoch) as album_published_epoch by trip_name
| eval lag_days=round((album_published_epoch-last_photo)/86400,1)
| sort - lag_days
description: Measures how long after a trip ends it takes for the album or shared memory package to be published.
value: Trips are more memorable when processed while the context is still fresh; lag highlights where curation drifts.
implementation: Capture album publish timestamps on trip photos and compare them with the trip's last photo time.
visualization: Table of trips with album completion lag in days.
grandmaExplanation: It warns how long travel photos sit around before you actually turn them into a finished album.
